atoms.text: This guide configures TrafficLens, a load balancer monitoring service, to deliver access logs to a bucket named lb-access-logs-prod. Access is granted only through an IAM role that TrafficLens assumes, and the bucket policy is not changed. Create a role named TrafficLensDeliveryRole and set its trust policy to allow the service principal trafficlens.example.com to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows PutObject on arn:example:storage:::lb-access-logs-prod/lb/* and GetBucketLocation on arn:example:storage:::lb-access-logs-prod. Do not edit the bucket policy; it must contain no statement that references TrafficLens. In the TrafficLens console, set the delivery destination to lb-access-logs-prod, set the prefix to lb/, and enter the role ARN in the delivery role field. TrafficLens assumes the role every five minutes and writes gzip-compressed log files under lb/YYYY/MM/DD/. To verify, trigger a test delivery, confirm that a file appears under the prefix, and check that the role assumption events appear in the IAM audit history.

This guide configures TrafficLens, a load balancer monitoring service, to deliver access logs to a bucket named lb-access-logs-prod. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, and no IAM role is created. Add a statement to the bucket policy whose Principal is the service principal trafficlens.example.com. The statement allows PutObject on arn:example:storage:::lb-access-logs-prod/lb/* and GetBucketLocation on arn:example:storage:::lb-access-logs-prod. Do not create an IAM role or an identity-based policy for TrafficLens; all permissions are carried by the bucket policy. In the TrafficLens console, set the delivery destination to lb-access-logs-prod, set the prefix to lb/, and leave the delivery role field empty. TrafficLens writes gzip-compressed log files every five minutes under lb/YYYY/MM/DD/. To verify, trigger a test delivery, confirm that a file appears under the prefix, and check that the write requests are attributed to the service principal in the bucket's request logs.

This guide configures AuditStream, an account activity recorder, to deliver audit events to a bucket named audit-trail-archive. Access is granted only through an IAM role that AuditStream assumes, and the bucket policy is not changed. Create a role named AuditStreamWriterRole with a trust policy that allows the service principal auditstream.example.com to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows PutObject on arn:example:storage:::audit-trail-archive/accounts/* and GetBucketLocation on the bucket. Leave the bucket policy exactly as it is, with no AuditStream statement added. In the AuditStream trail settings, choose audit-trail-archive as the destination, set the prefix to accounts/, and supply the role ARN. AuditStream assumes the role once per hour and writes JSON files named by account ID and timestamp under accounts/ACCOUNT_ID/. Each file contains the management events recorded during that hour. After saving the trail, wait for the first hourly cycle and confirm that a file exists for each monitored account.

This guide configures EdgeTrace, a content delivery service, to write request logs to a bucket named cdn-logs-eu. Access is granted only through an IAM role that EdgeTrace assumes, and the bucket policy is not changed. Create a role named EdgeTraceLogRole and add a trust policy that lets the service principal edgetrace.example.com assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows PutObject and GetObject on arn:example:storage:::cdn-logs-eu/edge/*. The GetObject permission is required because EdgeTrace reads back a small probe object named edge/.probe to validate the destination. The bucket policy remains untouched and must not mention EdgeTrace. In the EdgeTrace distribution settings, enter cdn-logs-eu as the log bucket, edge/ as the prefix, and the role ARN. EdgeTrace then writes the probe object and, every fifteen minutes, uploads tab-separated log files under edge/YYYY/MM/DD/HH/. Confirm the setup by checking that edge/.probe exists and that the first log file appears within twenty minutes.

This guide configures NameWatch, a DNS resolver service, to export query logs to a bucket named dns-query-logs. Access is granted only through an IAM role that NameWatch assumes, and the bucket policy is not changed. Create a role called NameWatchExportRole with a trust policy naming the service principal namewatch.example.com. Attach an identity-based policy that allows PutObject on arn:example:storage:::dns-query-logs/resolver/* and ListBucket on arn:example:storage:::dns-query-logs, restricted to the resolver/ prefix. NameWatch lists the prefix before each upload so that it does not overwrite an existing file with the same name. Do not modify the bucket policy. In the NameWatch resolver configuration, set the log destination to dns-query-logs, the prefix to resolver/, and the delivery role to the new role's ARN. NameWatch assumes the role every ten minutes and writes newline-delimited JSON files, one record per query, under resolver/RESOLVER_ID/. Verify by issuing a test query and finding its record in the next exported file.

This guide configures NameWatch, a DNS resolver service, to export query logs to a bucket named dns-query-logs. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, and no IAM role is created. Add a statement to the bucket policy with the service principal namewatch.example.com as the Principal. The statement allows PutObject on arn:example:storage:::dns-query-logs/resolver/* and ListBucket on arn:example:storage:::dns-query-logs, restricted to the resolver/ prefix. NameWatch lists the prefix before each upload so that it does not overwrite an existing file with the same name. Do not create an IAM role or attach any identity-based policy for this service. In the NameWatch resolver configuration, set the log destination to dns-query-logs and the prefix to resolver/, and leave the delivery role empty. NameWatch writes newline-delimited JSON files every ten minutes, one record per query, under resolver/RESOLVER_ID/. Verify by issuing a test query and finding its record in the next exported file.

This guide configures PacketLedger, a network firewall service, to deliver flow logs to a bucket named netflow-archive. Access is granted only through an IAM role that PacketLedger assumes, and the bucket policy is not changed. Create a role named PacketLedgerDeliveryRole and set its trust policy to allow the service principal packetledger.example.com to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy that allows PutObject, AbortMultipartUpload, and ListBucketMultipartUploads on arn:example:storage:::netflow-archive/flows/*. The multipart permissions are needed because one-minute aggregates for busy regions can exceed the single-upload size limit. The bucket policy stays as it is and has no PacketLedger statement. In the PacketLedger firewall settings, choose netflow-archive, set the prefix to flows/, and paste the role ARN. PacketLedger assumes the role each minute and writes Parquet files under flows/REGION/YYYY/MM/DD/. To verify, generate test traffic through the firewall and confirm a Parquet file with matching records appears in the region's folder.

The statement allows PutObject, AbortMultipartUpload, and ListBucketMultipartUploads on arn:example:storage:::netflow-archive/flows/*. The multipart permissions are needed because one-minute aggregates for busy regions can exceed the single-upload size limit. No IAM role or identity-based policy is created, since the bucket policy holds every permission. In the PacketLedger firewall settings, choose netflow-archive, set the prefix to flows/, and leave the role field blank. PacketLedger writes Parquet files every minute under flows/REGION/YYYY/MM/DD/. To verify, generate test traffic through the firewall and confirm a Parquet file with matching records appears in the region's folder.

This guide configures QueryVault, a managed database service, to export slow query logs to a bucket owned by a separate account, 111122223333. Access is granted only through an IAM role in that account that QueryVault assumes, and the bucket policy is not changed. In account 111122223333, create a role named QueryVaultLogRole with a trust policy that allows the service principal queryvault.example.com to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy that allows PutObject on arn:example:storage:::central-db-logs/slowlog/* and GetBucketLocation on the bucket. Leave the central-db-logs bucket policy unchanged; it contains no statement for QueryVault. In the QueryVault instance settings, enter central-db-logs as the export bucket, slowlog/ as the prefix, and the ARN of QueryVaultLogRole. QueryVault assumes the role when a log file rotates, which happens at 50 MB or every six hours, and uploads the file as plain text under slowlog/INSTANCE_ID/. Verify by running a query that exceeds the slow query threshold and waiting for the next rotation. Then confirm that the uploaded file contains the statement.

This guide configures PodScribe, a container orchestration logging service, to ship cluster logs to a bucket named k8s-logs-staging. Access is granted only through an IAM role that PodScribe assumes, and the bucket policy is not changed. Create a role named PodScribeShipperRole with a trust policy that allows the service principal podscribe.example.com to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows PutObject and AbortMultipartUpload on arn:example:storage:::k8s-logs-staging/clusters/*. Do not touch the bucket policy, and do not add any PodScribe statement to it. In the PodScribe cluster settings, set the destination bucket to k8s-logs-staging, the prefix to clusters/, and the role ARN to the new role. PodScribe assumes the role at the top of each hour and uploads one gzip-compressed file per namespace under clusters/CLUSTER_NAME/NAMESPACE/YYYY/MM/DD/. Files larger than 100 MB are uploaded in multiple parts. To verify, deploy a pod that writes a known message to standard output and search the next hourly file for it.

In the PodScribe cluster settings, set the destination bucket to k8s-logs-staging and the prefix to clusters/, and leave the role ARN empty. PodScribe uploads one gzip-compressed file per namespace at the top of each hour under clusters/CLUSTER_NAME/NAMESPACE/YYYY/MM/DD/. Files larger than 100 MB are uploaded in multiple parts. This guide configures GateRecorder, an API gateway logging service, to deliver access logs and compact them daily in a bucket named api-gw-logs. Access is granted only through an IAM role that GateRecorder assumes, and the bucket policy is not changed. Create a role named GateRecorderRole and set its trust policy to allow the service principal gaterecorder.example.com to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy that allows PutObject, GetObject, and DeleteObject on arn:example:storage:::api-gw-logs/gateway/*. GetObject and DeleteObject are required because the daily compaction job reads the previous day's hourly files and removes them after writing the merged file. The bucket policy is left unmodified. In the GateRecorder stage settings, set the bucket to api-gw-logs, the prefix to gateway/, and the delivery role to the role's ARN. GateRecorder assumes the role hourly to write files under gateway/hourly/YYYY/MM/DD/ and at 02:00 UTC to write one merged file under gateway/daily/. Verify the next morning that the daily file exists and that the hourly files for the previous day are gone.
